question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\pi}{36}}^{\frac{\pi}{36}} 8\cos\left(6 x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=6 x + \frac{\pi}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{36}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(- \frac{\pi}{36}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{36}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(\frac{\pi}{36}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{- \frac{\pi}{36}}^{\frac{\pi}{36}} 8\cos\left(6 x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=8\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left(\left(1\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{2}{3}} \sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{\pi x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\pi}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{\pi}{2}\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)=0\\ x=\frac{2}{3}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{\pi}{2}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{2}{3}} \sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=1\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{2}{\pi}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\\ &=- \frac{2}{\pi}\left(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)-\cos\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{2}{\pi}\left(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{1}{\pi}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{4 \pi}{9}}^{\frac{8 \pi}{9}} 8\sin\left(\frac{3 x}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{3 x}{4}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{3}{4},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{4 \pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{4 \pi}{9}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}\\ x=\frac{8 \pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{8 \pi}{9}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{4 \pi}{9}}^{\frac{8 \pi}{9}} 8\sin\left(\frac{3 x}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=8\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{32}{3}\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{32}{3}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}}\\ &=- \frac{32}{3}\left(\cos\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)-\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{32}{3}\left(\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{32}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{\pi}{9}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{9}} 4\sin\left(3 x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=3 x - \frac{\pi}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=3,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=3\left(\frac{\pi}{9}\right)+\left(- \frac{\pi}{3}\right)=0\\ x=\frac{2 \pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=3\left(\frac{2 \pi}{9}\right)+\left(- \frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{\pi}{9}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{9}} 4\sin\left(3 x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=4\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}\\ &=- \frac{4}{3}\left(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)-\cos\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{4}{3}\left(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{3}} 7\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{\pi x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\pi}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{\pi}{2}\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)=0\\ x=\frac{1}{3}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{\pi}{2}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{3}} 7\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=7\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{14}{\pi}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{14}{\pi}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\\ &=\frac{14}{\pi}\left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\sin\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{14}{\pi}\left(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{7}{\pi}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} 9\cos\left(\frac{2 x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{2 x}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{2}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{4}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{2}{3}\left(- \frac{\pi}{4}\right)+\left(0\right)=- \frac{\pi}{6}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{4}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{- \frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} 9\cos\left(\frac{2 x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=9\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\int_{- \frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{27}{2}\int_{- \frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{27}{2}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{- \frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\\ &=\frac{27}{2}\left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\sin\left(- \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{27}{2}\left(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{27}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
